title: Thermae · the published plan
figure: Avramova 2024, Fig. 24 (digital p. 280 / printed p. 276), based on Nikolov 1968: 44, fig. 1
scope: The recorded architecture of Fig. 24: solid-black masonry, clearly bounded hatched fabric around spaces 9–14 and the northern enclosure, the catchment’s square footprints, the three basin floors and readable stepped edges. Black and hatched conventions remain visually distinct without assigning construction phases. Source numbers are retained; broken-line water installations, arches and labels stay in the flat source plate.
limitation: A source-proportional plan relief. Raised shapes and colour are display conventions, not ancient wall height, surviving height, depth, water level or a shared floor level. Catchment 6 was underground. No roofs, arches, missing walls or phase chronology are reconstructed. Black ink has no explicit phase key in this figure. Copper ribbon width is a display convention, not wall thickness; these lines reproduce basin-edge drafting, not measured stair risers. The prose and the drawing describe the stepped sides differently, so no 3D step count or height is inferred. Raster boundary uncertainty is approximately ±3 pixels.

features.label: Masonry recorded in solid black
features.note: Outer and inner edges, openings, detached semicircular feature 8, and breaks in the central wall are retained from the black-ink plan. No phase attribution is inferred.

features.label: Catchment 6 · column footprints
features.note: Printed p. 58 identifies 6 as an underground catchment with brick columns supporting arches. The detached marks follow their recorded size and rotation. Where a mark touches the circled number 6, only the square footprint is retained. Attached perimeter projections remain in the solid-black masonry feature. No arch or vertical relationship is reconstructed.

features.label: Pool 1
features.note: Inner floor area read directly against the innermost drawn basin boundary. The colour identifies the basin floor footprint, not water, a reconstructed depth, or a common elevation. Edge irregularities and the open northern interruption of pool 1 are preserved where legible.

features.label: Pool 2
features.note: Inner floor area read directly against the innermost drawn basin boundary. The colour identifies the floor, not water, a reconstructed depth or a common elevation.

features.label: Pool 5
features.note: Inner floor area read directly against the innermost drawn basin boundary. The colour identifies the floor, not water, a reconstructed depth or a common elevation.

features.label: Square mark inside the semicircular feature
features.note: The separate rotated black square inside the small semicircular feature adjoining catchment 6 is copied from Fig. 24 without assigning it a new function or a height.

features.label: Basin edges and step lines
features.note: Thin 1.5-pixel display ribbons copy the readable basin contours in Fig. 24. They preserve the northern interruption at pool 1 and distinguish floor area from the surrounding bands. Printed p. 81 gives step counts whose long/short-side wording appears reversed relative to this plate, so these source lines are not converted into measured risers or assigned a stair count.

features.label: Enclosure & spaces 9–14
features.note: Both edges are legible in these hatched bands: the northern enclosure, space 9 and the southern connection, and the eastern range of numbered spaces 10–14. Open approaches, the interruption beside 13, interior voids and the rounded southern end of 13 are preserved. This is a distinct graphic convention in Fig. 24; no phase, construction material or wall height is assigned.

independentReview.method: Independently compared complete plate, original raster, enlarged contours and source descriptions. Rotated footprints and basin corners were checked visually, not inferred from existing JSON. Photographs were reviewed for relevance, not used to invent elevations.
